answer_1.quote: Question Generation (QG) aims to generate questions from diverse inputs, including text, knowledge base, and so on.
answer_1.outputs: conversational questions to guide interactions toward specified outcomes

answer_2.quote: We employ widely used evaluation metrics for text generation, including BLEU and METEOR, to evaluate the generated response. Concretely, BLEU evaluates the precision of the generated text compared to the reference text. METEOR is a detailed evaluation considering exact words, synonyms, and similar phrases. Additionally, we employ SimCSE to measure conversational coherence. ... Furthermore, the most pivotal metric is the Success Rate

answer_4.quote: Due to the extensive critique of automatic metrics for their poor alignment with human assessments, we incorporate two human evaluation metrics: Coherence and Effectiveness. We randomly select 50 conversations from the validation set of the CoQA dataset and invite three individuals to score the generated responses, with a scoring range of {0, 1, 2}, where a higher score indicates better quality in terms of Coherence and Effectiveness.
answer_4.guideline: Coherence assesses whether the entire conversation maintains logical and topic coherence, while Effectiveness assesses the efficiency with which the intended conversational outcome is achieved.
